content: A hangnail, also known as an agnail, refers to a small, torn piece of skin that occurs near the edge of a fingernail or toenail. This condition is typically caused by dry skin or, in the case of fingernails, by nail-biting. Proper moisturization of the skin can help prevent the development of hangnails. When attempting to remove a hangnail, it is important to do so carefully. If the hangnail is not properly detached, additional skin may be torn away, which can be painful. This improper removal can also lead to a bacterial infection known as paronychia. To avoid such complications, hangnails should be trimmed using nail scissors or a nail clipper. Biting hangnails often exacerbates the problem and should be avoided. It is worth noting that the term hangnail is somewhat misleading, as it does not refer to the nail itself. Instead, a hangnail is composed of dead, dried skin, whereas the nail is primarily made of calcium and keratin, a fibrous protein. The term agnail originates from Middle English and was used to describe a corn on the foot. It is derived from the Old English word angnægl, which combines ang(meaning tight or painful) and nægl (meaning nail). Over time, the term evolved into hangnail through a process of folk etymology.
